## Introduction

```{r Setup}
options(scipen=999) #turns off scientific notation for numbers. 
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.width=12, fig.height=8) #knit to word, pdf  chops titles and graphs without setting the figure size as the global option.

library(rpart)
library(rpart.plot)
library(caret)
library(readxl)
library(writexl)
library(tidyverse)
setwd("C:\\Users\\star-\\Data Science\\R stuff\\D.comm")

#import statements
#modeldf<-read.csv("C:\\Users\\star-\\Data Science\\R stuff\\D.comm\\modeldf.csv")
modeldf<-read_xlsx("C:\\Users\\star-\\Data Science\\R stuff\\D.comm\\modeldf.xlsx")
summary(modeldf$Associates)
summary(modeldf$Bachelors)
summary(modeldf$Masters)
summary(modeldf$Doctoral)

#modeldf<-df2
df<-modeldf|>
  mutate(
    Associates_Percent = (Associates/`Student Count`)*100,
    Bachelors_Percent = (Bachelors/`Student Count`)*100,
    Masters_Percent = (Masters/`Student Count`)*100,
    Doctoral_Percent = (Doctoral/`Student Count`)*100
  )|>filter(Masters_Percent<80)
summary(df$Associates)
summary(df$Bachelors)
summary(df$Masters)
summary(df$Doctoral)
summary(df$Associates_Percent)
summary(df$Bachelors_Percent)
summary(df$Masters_Percent)
summary(df$Doctoral_Percent)

#write_xlsx(df,"visualdf.xlsx")

```

## Assumption Checking

### QQplots

```{r QQplots}
#table(df2)
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
qqnorm(df2$Associates_Percent,main="Figure 3: QQ plot of Associates degrees",pch=19,
       cex.main=1.2)
#Add a line where x = y to help assess how closely the scatter fits the line.
qqline(df2$Associates_Percent)

qqnorm(df2$Bachelors_Percent,main="Figure 4: QQ plot of Bachelors degrees",pch=19,
       cex.main=1.2)
#Add a line where x = y to help assess how closely the scatter fits the line.
qqline(df2$Bachelors_Percent)

qqnorm(df2$Masters_Percent,main="Figure 5: QQ plot of Masters degrees",pch=19,
       cex.main=1.2)
#Add a line where x = y to help assess how closely the scatter fits the line.
qqline(df2$Masters_Percent)

qqnorm(df2$Doctoral_Percent,main="Figure 6: QQ plot of Doctoral degrees",pch=19,
       cex.main=1.2)
#Add a line where x = y to help assess how closely the scatter fits the line.
qqline(df2$Doctoral_Percent)

#reset back to one by one graphic
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```


## Two-sample T-test

### In vs Out of State Tuition

```{r In/Out state tuition}

t<-t.test(df$`In-State Tuition`,df$`Out-of-State Tutition`,data=df, alternative ="two.sided",
          mu = 0, var.equal = TRUE, conf.level = .95)
t #the full results
t$p.value #gets the pvalue
t$conf.int # gets the confidence interval

t<-t.test(df$`In-State Tuition`,df$`Out-of-State Tutition`,data=df, alternative ="two.sided",
          mu = 0, var.equal = FALSE, conf.level = .95)
t #the full results
t$p.value #gets the pvalue
t$conf.int # gets the confidence interval
```

```{r Nonpara Tuition}
wil<-wilcox.test(df$`In-State Tuition`,df$`Out-of-State Tutition`,exact=FALSE,alternative="two.sided", conf.int = TRUE, conf.level=.95)

wil
round(wil$p.value*100,3)
```

### On vs Off Campus Housing

```{r "On/off Campus Housing"}
t<-t.test(df$`On-Campus Housing`,df$`Off-Campus Housing`,data=df, alternative ="two.sided",           mu = 0, var.equal = TRUE, conf.level = .95) 
t #the full results 
t$p.value #gets the pvalue 
t$conf.int # gets the confidence interval 

t<-t.test(df$`On-Campus Housing`,df$`Off-Campus Housing`,data=df, alternative ="two.sided",           mu = 0, var.equal = FALSE, conf.level = .95) 
t #the full results 
t$p.value #gets the pvalue 
t$conf.int # gets the confidence interval  


wil<-wilcox.test(df$`On-Campus Housing`,df$`Off-Campus Housing`,exact=FALSE,alternative="two.sided", conf.int = TRUE, conf.level=.95)

wil
round(wil$p.value*100,3)

summary(df$`On-Campus Housing`)
summary(df$`Off-Campus Housing`)
```

### On vs Off Campus vs Family Expenses

```{r On/off/family expenses}
df_long <- df %>%
  select(`Family Expenses`, `On-Campus Expenses`, `Off-Campus Expenses`) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(), 
    names_to = "housing_type",
    values_to = "score"
  ) %>%
  drop_na(score) %>%
  mutate(housing_type = as.factor(housing_type))

Ratio_of_MaxToMin_SD <- function(quant,categ){
  temp<-tapply(quant,categ,FUN=sd)
  ratio<-round(max(temp)/min(temp),2)
  #return(temp)
  print("The standard deviations of the quantitative variable for the different categorical levels are:")
  print(temp)
  print(paste("The ratio of the largest standard deviation to the smallest standard deviation is:", ratio))
}

# Call Statement for the Function to check if the ratio of the largest standard deviation to the smalles standard deviation is less than 2, the rule of thumb for being able to pool.
Ratio_of_MaxToMin_SD(df_long$score,df_long$housing_type)
#glimpse(df_long)
print("The average expenses for on-campus students:")
print(paste(round(mean(df_long$score[df_long$housing_type=="On-Campus Expenses"]),2), sep = ""))

print("The average expenses for off-campus students:")
print(paste(round(mean(df_long$score[df_long$housing_type=="Off-Campus Expenses"]),2), sep = ""))

print("The average expenses for students living at home:")
print(paste(round(mean(df_long$score[df_long$housing_type=="Family Expenses"]),2), sep = ""))
# Run a standard Between-Subjects One-Way ANOVA
anova_model <- aov(score ~ housing_type, data = df_long)
krusk_model<- kruskal.test(score ~ housing_type, data = df_long) 

# View the summary
summary(anova_model)
krusk_model

TukeyHSD(anova_model)
pairwise.t.test(df_long$score, df_long$housing_type, p.adj  = "bonferroni") 

#nonpara post hoc
pairwise_result <- pairwise.wilcox.test(df_long$score, df_long$housing_type, p.adjust.method = "bonferroni")
print(pairwise_result)
```

```{r}
df %>%
  select(`Family Expenses`, `On-Campus Expenses`, `Off-Campus Expenses`) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = value, fill = variable)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 25, color = "white", alpha = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free") +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Expense Types",
    x = "Amount",
    y = "Count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

What we learned: out of state tuition is more expensive then in-state tuition, there is no difference in housing costs for student on or off campus; however, students on-campus have less expenses then both off-campus students and students living at home.

## Linear Models

```{r Linear Models}
linear.model <- lm(Associates_Percent ~`In-State Tuition`+ `Out-of-State Tutition`+ `Supply Costs`+`On-Campus Housing`+ `On-Campus Expenses`+ `Off-Campus Housing`+
                     `Off-Campus Expenses`+ `Family Expenses`
                   , data=df)
summary(linear.model)

linear.model2 <- lm(Bachelors_Percent ~`In-State Tuition`+ `Out-of-State Tutition`+ `Supply Costs`+`On-Campus Housing`+ `On-Campus Expenses`+ `Off-Campus Housing`+
                     `Off-Campus Expenses`+ `Family Expenses`
                   , data=df)
summary(linear.model2)

linear.model3 <- lm(Masters_Percent ~`In-State Tuition`+ `Out-of-State Tutition`+ `Supply Costs`+`On-Campus Housing`+ `On-Campus Expenses`+ `Off-Campus Housing`+
                     `Off-Campus Expenses`+ `Family Expenses`
                   , data=df)
summary(linear.model3)
linear.model4 <- lm(Doctoral ~`In-State Tuition`+ `Out-of-State Tutition`+ `Supply Costs`+`On-Campus Housing`+ `On-Campus Expenses`+ `Off-Campus Housing`+
                     `Off-Campus Expenses`+ `Family Expenses`
                   , data=df)
summary(linear.model4)
```

## Model 1 and 2: Tree and KNN

### Associates

```{r Associates Split}
df_filter<-df|>filter(Associates_Percent>0)|> select(Associates_Percent,`In-State Tuition`, `Out-of-State Tutition`, `Supply Costs`, `On-Campus Housing`, `On-Campus Expenses`, `Off-Campus Housing`, `Off-Campus Expenses`, `Family Expenses`)|>drop_na()

# test-train split
set.seed(394)


df_trn_idx = sample(nrow(df_filter), size = 0.8 * nrow(df_filter))
df_trn = df_filter[df_trn_idx, ]
df_tst = df_filter[-df_trn_idx, ]
# estimation-validation split
df_est_idx = sample(nrow(df_trn), size = 0.8 * nrow(df_trn))
df_est = df_trn[df_est_idx, ]
df_val = df_trn[-df_est_idx, ]


# check data
head(df_trn, n = 10)

calc_rmse = function(actual, predicted) {
  sqrt(mean((actual - predicted) ^ 2))
}
```

```{r Tree Associates}
library(rpart)
library(randomforest)
library(rpart.plot)
library(caret)
tree <- rpart(Associates_Percent ~`In-State Tuition`+ `Out-of-State Tutition`+ `Supply Costs`+`On-Campus Housing`+ `On-Campus Expenses`+ `Off-Campus Housing`+
                `Off-Campus Expenses`+ `Family Expenses`, data=df_est, control=rpart.control(cp=.0001))
printcp(tree)

rpart.plot(tree)

#identify best cp value to use
best <- tree$cptable[which.min(tree$cptable[,"xerror"]),"CP"]
best
#produce a pruned tree based on the best cp value
pruned_tree <- prune(tree, cp=best)

#plot the pruned tree
prp(pruned_tree,
    faclen=0, #use full names for factor labels
    extra=1, #display number of obs. for each terminal node
    roundint=F, #don't round to integers in output
    digits=5) #display 5 decimal places in output


tree_mod_list = list(
  tree_0000 <- rpart(Associates_Percent ~`In-State Tuition`+ `Out-of-State Tutition`+ `Supply Costs`+`On-Campus Housing`+ `On-Campus Expenses`+ `Off-Campus Housing`+`Off-Campus Expenses`+ `Family Expenses`, data=df_est, control=rpart.control(cp=.0000)),
  tree_0001 <- rpart(Associates_Percent ~`In-State Tuition`+ `Out-of-State Tutition`+ `Supply Costs`+`On-Campus Housing`+ `On-Campus Expenses`+ `Off-Campus Housing`+ `Off-Campus Expenses`+ `Family Expenses`, data=df_est, control=rpart.control(cp=.0001)),
  tree_0010 <- rpart(Associates_Percent ~`In-State Tuition`+ `Out-of-State Tutition`+ `Supply Costs`+`On-Campus Housing`+ `On-Campus Expenses`+ `Off-Campus Housing`+`Off-Campus Expenses`+ `Family Expenses`, data=df_est, control=rpart.control(cp=.0010)),
  tree_0100 <- rpart(Associates_Percent ~`In-State Tuition`+ `Out-of-State Tutition`+ `Supply Costs`+`On-Campus Housing`+ `On-Campus Expenses`+ `Off-Campus Housing`+`Off-Campus Expenses`+ `Family Expenses`, data=df_est, control=rpart.control(cp=.0100))
)

tree_val_pred = lapply(tree_mod_list, predict, df_val)

sapply(tree_val_pred, calc_rmse, df_val$Associates_Percent)
crdt_tree_all = rpart(Associates_Percent ~ ., data = df_est)
rpart.plot(crdt_tree_all)

predict(crdt_tree_all, df_val[1:5, ])
```

```{r Associates KNN}
x<- df_val|>select(-Associates_Percent)
y <- df_val$Associates_Percent

any(is.na(x))

# Fit the KNN regression model
df_knn_15 <- knnreg(x = x, y = y,data=df_est, k = 15)
knn_mod_list = list(
  df_knn_5 <- knnreg(x = x, y = y,data=df_est, k = 5),
  df_knn_10 <- knnreg(x = x, y = y,data=df_est, k = 10),
  df_knn_15<-df_knn_15,
  df_knn_25 <- knnreg(x = x, y = y,data=df_est, k = 25),
  df_knn_50 <- knnreg(x = x, y = y,data=df_est, k = 50),
  df_knn_100 <- knnreg(x = x, y = y,data=df_est, k = 100)
)
head(df_knn_15$learn$X)
dist(head(df_knn_15$learn$X))


#predict(df_knn_10, df_val[1:5, ])
x_val <- df_val |> select(-Associates_Percent)
#glimpse(x_est)
knn_val_pred = lapply(knn_mod_list, predict, x_val)
calc_rmse = function(actual, predicted) {
  sqrt(mean((actual - predicted) ^ 2))
}

sapply(knn_val_pred, calc_rmse, df_val$Associates_Percent)
```

```{r Bachelors Tree}
)
```

```{r Bachelors KNN}
sapply(knn_val_pred, calc_rmse, df_val$Bachelors_Percent)
```

```{r Masters KNN}
  df_knn_100 <- knnreg(x = x, y = y,data=df_est, k = 100)
)
head(df_knn_15$learn$X)
dist(head(df_knn_15$learn$X))


#predict(df_knn_10, df_val[1:5, ])
x_val <- df_val |> select(-Masters_Percent)
#glimpse(x_est)
knn_val_pred = lapply(knn_mod_list, predict, x_val)
calc_rmse = function(actual, predicted) {
  sqrt(mean((actual - predicted) ^ 2))
}

sapply(knn_val_pred, calc_rmse, df_val$Masters_Percent)
```

### Doctoral

```{r Doctoral}
df_filter<-df|>filter(Doctoral_Percent>0)|> select(Doctoral_Percent,`In-State Tuition`, `Out-of-State Tutition`, `Supply Costs`, `On-Campus Housing`, `On-Campus Expenses`, `Off-Campus Housing`, `Off-Campus Expenses`, `Family Expenses`)|>drop_na()

# test-train split
set.seed(394)


df_trn_idx = sample(nrow(df_filter), size = 0.8 * nrow(df_filter))

df_tst = df_filter[-df_trn_idx, ]
# estimation-validation split

df_val = df_trn[-df_est_idx, ]


# check data
head(df_trn, n = 10)
```

```{r Doctoral Tree}
tree <- rpart(Doctoral_Percent ~`In-State Tuition`+ `Out-of-State Tutition`+ `Supply Costs`+`On-Campus Housing`+ `On-Campus Expenses`+ `Off-Campus Housing`+
                `Off-Campus Expenses`+ `Family Expenses`, data=df_est, control=rpart.control(cp=.0100))
printcp(tree)

rpart.plot(tree)

#identify best cp value to use
best <- tree$cptable[which.min(tree$cptable[,"xerror"]),"CP"]
best
#produce a pruned tree based on the best cp value
pruned_tree <- prune(tree, cp=best)

#plot the pruned tree
prp(pruned_tree,
    faclen=0, #use full names for factor labels
    extra=1, #display number of obs. for each terminal node
    roundint=F, #don't round to integers in output
    digits=5) #display 5 decimal places in output


tree_mod_list = list(
  tree_0000 <- rpart(Doctoral_Percent ~`In-State Tuition`+ `Out-of-State Tutition`+ `Supply Costs`+`On-Campus Housing`+ `On-Campus Expenses`+ `Off-Campus Housing`+`Off-Campus Expenses`+ `Family Expenses`, data=df_est, control=rpart.control(cp=.0000)),
  tree_0001 <- rpart(Doctoral_Percent ~`In-State Tuition`+ `Out-of-State Tutition`+ `Supply Costs`+`On-Campus Housing`+ `On-Campus Expenses`+ `Off-Campus Housing`+ `Off-Campus Expenses`+ `Family Expenses`, data=df_est, control=rpart.control(cp=.0001)),
  tree_0010 <- rpart(Doctoral_Percent ~`In-State Tuition`+ `Out-of-State Tutition`+ `Supply Costs`+`On-Campus Housing`+ `On-Campus Expenses`+ `Off-Campus Housing`+`Off-Campus Expenses`+ `Family Expenses`, data=df_est, control=rpart.control(cp=.0010)),
  tree_0100 <- rpart(Doctoral_Percent ~`In-State Tuition`+ `Out-of-State Tutition`+ `Supply Costs`+`On-Campus Housing`+ `On-Campus Expenses`+ `Off-Campus Housing`+`Off-Campus Expenses`+ `Family Expenses`, data=df_est, control=rpart.control(cp=.0100))
)

tree_val_pred = lapply(tree_mod_list, predict, df_val)

sapply(tree_val_pred, calc_rmse, df_val$Doctoral_Percent)
crdt_tree_all = rpart(Doctoral_Percent ~ ., data = df_est)
rpart.plot(crdt_tree_all)

predict(crdt_tree_all, df_val[1:5, ])
```

# Further Model Building

## Clusters

```{r Fuzzy Clustering}
#install.packages("e1071")
#install.packages("factoextra")

library(e1071)
library(factoextra)
glimpse(df)
datas<-df|> select(!Associates:Doctoral & !Institution)
data<-na.omit(datas)
glimpse(data)
```

```{r cluster creation}
#cluster creation with 4 clusters
set.seed(934)
n_cluster <- 4
m <- 2
result <- cmeans(data, centers = n_cluster, m = m)

fuzzy_membership_matrix <- result$membership
clusters <- as.factor(result$cluster)

initial_centers <- result$centers
final_centers <- t(result$centers)
```

```{r cluster visual}
#Method 1 visualization
fviz_cluster(list(data = data, cluster = clusters),
             geom = "point",
             ellipse.type = "convex",
             main = "Fuzzy C-Means Clustering on mtcars Dataset")
#method 2 heads
cluster_membership <- as.data.frame(result$membership)
data_with_clusters <- cbind(data, cluster_membership)
head(data_with_clusters)

```

### Cluster quality

```{r gapstat}
library(cluster)

gap_stat <- clusGap(data, FUN = kmeans, nstart = 25,
                    K.max = 10, B = 50)

print(gap_stat)

fviz_gap_stat(gap_stat)
```

### **Davies-Bouldin Index**

```{r Davies-Bouldin Index}
#install.packages("clusterSim")
library(clusterSim)

set.seed(123)
km_res <- kmeans(data, centers = 5, nstart = 25)

db_index <- index.DB(data, km_res$cluster, centrotypes = "centroids")

print(db_index$DB)
```

### **Calinski-Harabasz Index**

```{r  Davies-Bouldin Index}
ch_index <- index.G1(data, km_res$cluster)

print(ch_index)
```

```{r}
data$Cluster <- apply(result$membership, 1, which.max)

ggplot(data, aes(x = Bachelors_Percent, y = `In-State Tuition`, color = as.factor(Cluster))) +

  labs(title = "Fuzzy C-means Clustering", x = "Percent of Bachelors Conferred", y = "In-State Tuition ($)")
```
